doc: wrap/ellipsise/terse cases were executed from the-bastion's frontend/src/render.ts (wrapLabel, terse are exported and were called directly; ellipsise is not exported and was executed from a verbatim one-line copy of its body) -- the house budget case (22 cols, 2 lines) is the shape frontend/src/render.test.mjs's own fixture wraps at. lineCount is DEFINED as wrap's own uncapped line count (see geometry.ts's doc comment on lineCount), so every lineCount case here is wrap(text, cols, Infinity).length on the SAME text/cols pairs as the wrap cases above -- not the-bastion's backend/layout.py _text_lines(), which was executed too and used only to CHECK agreement. It agreed on 6 of 8; on the other two, _text_lines is a pre-existing bug this module deliberately does not carry forward, flagged here for the Python-half implementer: an empty string (_text_lines counts 1 line where wrap draws 0), and a single word longer than the column budget ('antidisestablishmentarianism' at 10 cols: _text_lines counts 2, assuming an overlong word always spills onto a second line, never accounting for wrap cutting that word with an ellipsis to fit on the first; wrap itself produces exactly 1 line). Both corrected cases say so in their own name.
